subject: Sizing input for AuroraAI pilot — traffic matrix & prompt mix
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@auroraai.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T14:22:00-04:00
Subject: Pilot sizing — initial traffic & goals

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team is excited to move to a short pilot. To get us unstuck on procurement and sizing, can you share a concise questionnaire we can fill out with our traffic profile and prompt/response characteristics? Our procurement team needs a ballpark GPU footprint to budget for a 6-week pilot. High level info from our side:

- Core use case: contextual customer support summarization + automated reply suggestions (real-time chat).
- Current expected daily requests during pilot: starting at ~5k/day, target up to 40k/day by week 4 (growth is bursty).
- Typical prompt: 120-350 tokens; typical response: 80-450 tokens depending on context.
- Peak hour expectation: 09:00–11:00 PT, where we expect ~40% of daily volume.
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for suggestion endpoint, <1200ms acceptable for full summarization.

Procurement also asked for: estimated monthly cost range, concurrency assumptions, and whether Redwood can support a pinned model variant during pilot. We can share sample logs (CSV) if helpful.

Would appreciate the sizing template and any initial fleet hypothesis you can provide.

Best,
Samir
Director of Product, AuroraAI

---
Attachments referenced: none in this message
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T16:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — initial traffic & goals

Hi Samir,

Thanks — this is helpful context. I've attached a short sizing-template.xlsx that focuses on the data points we need to produce a conservative fleet hypothesis (QPS by traffic class, prompt/response token distributions, cold vs warm session rates, and KV cache reuse). A few clarifying questions before the team builds the hypothesis:

1) Can you confirm the percent of calls that are short token completions (prompt+resp <= 200 tokens) versus long summarizations (>600 tokens)? A rough split is fine.
2) How many concurrent active chat sessions do you expect during peak hour (users actively typing and getting suggestions)?
3) Are sessions sticky to user KV (i.e., local KV cache reuse across messages)? If so, average KV size per session (approx tokens) would help.
4) Any hard limits on model variants (e.g., must use open-quantized variant vs larger unquantized model)?

Quick note on pinned models: yes, Redwood Dedicated can pin a model variant for the pilot. We recommend a quantized 8-bit variant for predictability unless you need the full FP16 behavior for quality. Marissa will follow up with an initial fleet hypothesis once we get your quick answers and the sample traffic.

I'll also include a conservative mapping: for chat suggestion endpoint (target p95=300ms), plan for 1.2–1.8 tokens/ms across optimized GPUs depending on sequence length and batching; this is a rough rule-of-thumb until we see your sample CSV.

Attached: sizing-template.xlsx

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: sizing-template.xlsx (spreadsheet): short form with QPS / token bins / concurrency fields
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — initial traffic & goals (initial fleet hypothesis)

Hi Samir — looping in a quick hypothesis based on the numbers you shared and some conservative assumptions. See below for the baseline pilot plan and attached PDF with a one-page fleet map.

Baseline assumptions (conservative):
- Avg prompt tokens: 200; avg response tokens: 220; mean combined = 420 tokens/call.
- 5k starting calls/day -> ~2.1M tokens/day; at 40k/day -> ~16.8M tokens/day.
- Peak hour (40% of daily) at 40k/day -> 16k calls in peak 2-hour window -> ~2.2 calls/sec average in peak (but bursty with short spikes).
- For p95=300ms on suggestion endpoint we assume optimized kernels on A100-class or equivalent GPUs; mapping: 1 GPU can handle ~450–600 suggestion QPS (shorter tokens / batching) or ~60–120 heavy summarization QPS depending on sequence length and whether KV cache hits occur.

Pilot fleet hypothesis (week 1 conservative):
- 1 dedicated node (2x GPUs) configured for mixed workload with autoscale policy to add spare GPUs for sustained bursts.
- Plan for burst buffer: allow 2–3x concurrent capacity during peak short spikes.
- Recommended model: quantized Llama-7B variant for suggestion path, full FP16 variant for nightly batch summarization if quality delta is meaningful.

Operational notes & asks:
- Please upload a 72-hour sample traffic CSV (timestamp, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, session_id) — that lets us compute true concurrency distributions and KV reuse.
- If you need strict p95 SLAs during the pilot we should size for the 95th percentile burst QPS, not the mean.

Costs: very rough pilot estimate (excluding data transfer/observability add-ons):
- Conservative monthly burn for pilot: $6k–$18k depending on autoscale behavior and model variant choices (quantized vs FP16).

Attached: initial-fleet-hypothesis.pdf (one-page mapping with GPU counts and cost bands)

Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the numbers — Jordan, if you want to propose times I can join.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: initial-fleet-hypothesis.pdf
From: Samir Patel <samir@auroraai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@auroraai.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing — initial traffic & goals (answers + sample)

Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks — attached is a 72-hour sample_traffic.csv and a short procurement timeline. Quick answers inline to your questions:

1) Short vs long split: ~65% short completions (<=200 tokens total), ~25% mid (201–600), ~10% long (>600).
2) Concurrent active chat sessions at peak: estimate 1,200 active sessions, but only ~18% of those trigger requests per minute. Rough peak concurrency for API calls estimated ~150–220 concurrent requests during the 09:00–11:00 window.
3) Sessions are sticky; KV reuse expected — average KV size ~3–4k tokens per session (context + recent history).
4) Model variant: preference for quantized variant during pilot; we will evaluate FP16 later if quality regressions appear.

Files attached: sample-traffic.csv, procurement-timeline.pdf

Next steps: we'll fill the sizing-template.xlsx you sent and aim to return it by EOD Monday. Also happy to schedule a 30 min sizing call with Marissa — proposed times: Mon 11:00–12:00 PT or Tue 09:00–10:00 PT.

Best,
Samir
Director of Product, AuroraAI

---
